rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.6 - one-season (2002) split-plot field experiment at PAU Bathinda, India, with three replications, measuring seed cotton yield, stick weight, growth parameters and water use. Q2: Section 3.1 and Table 4 - drip at the same water and N as check-basin gave 2144 vs 1624 kg/ha seed cotton (32% increase); at 75% water drip still yielded 12% more than check-basin; conclusions restate the 32% increase.
rows.notes: The passage attributes the finding to Ad El-wahed & Ali (2013) on maize, sprinkler vs drip, in Egypt; this cited study is instead cotton, drip vs check-basin (surface flooding), in Punjab, India, so the attribution and the comparator/crop do not match, though the technology (drip) and effect (higher yield) do. Q3: single method (plot yield harvest). Q4: growth parameters and profile water use are reported but no intermediate mechanism variable (e.g. soil water status under drip) is measured; dry-matter-allocation mechanism is cited from Mateos et al. Q5/Q6: one site, one soil (loamy sand), one crop, one season, plot scale. Q7: yield benefit found to depend on water and N level, but not stated as a requirement. Q8: no limitations stated beyond 'under these experimental conditions'. Q9: only LSD at 5% reported, no SD/SE/CI.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.6 - own replicated field experiment with measured irrigation water (Parshall flume for check-basin, metered drip at Epan ratios), profile water and rainfall (Table 6). Q2: Table 6, Table 7 and Section 3.2 - drip at 0.3 Epan applied 41.1 cm vs 54.6 cm in check-basin (25% less) with 12% higher yield; paired sowing under drip used 27.3 cm (50% saving) with 20% higher yield; WUE rose from 17.6 to 22.1 kg/ha cm (26%) under drip at equal water and to 27.3 under paired-sowing drip.
rows.notes: Passage misattributes the finding (names Ad El-wahed & Ali 2013, maize, sprinkler vs drip, Egypt); this study is cotton, drip vs check-basin, India; technology and effect match the claim. Q3: water saving and WUE derived from one method (applied water accounting plus plot yield). Q4: no measurement of the mechanism (e.g. percolation, soil evaporation); reduced percolation is asserted in conclusions, not measured. Q5/Q6: one site, soil, crop and season at plot scale. Q7: water saving without yield loss depends on paired sowing/water level, but not framed as a required condition. Q8: no limitation statement. Q9: LSD only, no dispersion measure for water use or WUE.

notes: Full text appears complete. The review passage describes a different study (Ad El-wahed & Ali 2013, maize, sprinkler vs drip, Egypt) but cites this cotton drip vs check-basin experiment from Bathinda, India; ratings reflect what this study itself shows about drip for yield and water saving.
